chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali Majiluwayh - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim, on the authority of al-Mukhtar ibn Muhammad ibn al-Mukhtar al-Hamadani, on the authority of al-Fath ibn Yazid al-Jurjani, on the authority of Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about the lowest degree of recognition,

He said: It is the acknowledgement that there is no god but Him, and there is no likeness to Him, and no equal to Him, and that He is Eternal, Established, Existing, never absent, and that there is nothing like Him.
ai.seo_question: What is the minimum requirement for recognizing God in Shia theology?
ai.summary: In this tradition from Imam al-Rida (AS), the foundational level of *ma'irah* (gnosis) is defined not merely as verbal declaration but as a profound theological affirmation of God's eternity (*Qadim*) and absolute existence (*Mawjud*) without deficiency (*Ghayr Faqid*). This definition aligns with the Shia scholarly emphasis on *Tawhid al-Dhat* (Unity of Essence), distinguishing the Divine from creation by negating any likeness (*Kaf' al-Mithl*), a concept central to the school of the Ahl al-Bayt. It serves as the prerequisite for deeper spiritual knowledge, grounding the believer's understanding in the absolute transcendence of God.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 11-29 Muhammad ibn Ali Majiluwayh - may God be pleased with him -narrated that Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashem quoted on the authority of al-Mokhtar ibn Muhammad al-Mokhtar al-Hamadani, on the authority of al-Fath ibn Yazid al-Gorgani, “I asked Abil Hassan (s), ‘What is the least degree of recognition?’

The Imam (s) replied, ‘It is the acknowledgement of God and that there is no other god; there is nothing like Him; there is nothing similar to Him; He is Stable, Eternal, Existing; He is never absent, and that there is nothing else like Him.’”
